title: 李凭箜篌引
title_en: Li Ping Plays the Konghou Harp
author: 李贺

text_note.zh: 语料库第二句作“空白凝云”，第五句作“凤皇呌”，第十一句作“坤山”。课本作“空山凝云”“凤凰叫”“神山”，这里按课本。“凤皇”就是“凤凰”，“呌”是“叫”的异体字。
text_note.en: The corpus has "kōng bái" (empty white) instead of "kōng shān" (empty hills) in line two, older ways of writing "fèng huáng jiào" in line five, and "kūn shān" instead of "shén shān" (the hills of the gods) in line eleven. This page follows the textbook.

readings.zh: 弹奏乐器的“弹”读 tán，不读 dàn。
readings.en: When it means to play an instrument, this character is read tán, not dàn.

readings.zh: “教”在这里是传授、教给的意思，读 jiāo。
readings.en: Here this character means to teach someone, so it is read jiāo.

glosses.zh: 吴丝蜀桐：吴地出产的蚕丝做琴弦，蜀地出产的桐木做琴身。说明这把箜篌用料极好。
glosses.en: wú sī shǔ tóng: strings of silk from Wu and a body of tung wood from Shu. The harp is made of the finest materials.

glosses.zh: 张：把弦绷紧，这里指弹奏。
glosses.en: zhāng: to stretch the strings tight, here meaning to start playing.

glosses.zh: 高秋：天高气爽的深秋。
glosses.en: gāo qiū: deep autumn, when the sky is high and clear.

glosses.zh: 凝云颓不流：天上的云听了音乐，像凝住了一样，低低地垂着不再飘动。颓，下垂。
glosses.en: níng yún tuí bù liú: the clouds, hearing the music, seem frozen; they hang low and stop drifting. Tuí means to droop.

glosses.zh: 江娥啼竹：江娥指舜的两个妃子娥皇、女英。传说舜死后她们哭泣，泪水洒在竹子上，留下斑点，成了斑竹。
glosses.en: jiāng é tí zhú: the river goddesses weep on the bamboo. Legend says the two wives of the ancient ruler Shun wept when he died, and their tears left spots on the bamboo.

glosses.zh: 素女：传说中善于弹瑟的神女。
glosses.en: sù nǚ: a goddess in legend who was good at playing the zither.

glosses.zh: 中国：国中，指京城长安城中，不是今天“中国”的意思。
glosses.en: zhōng guó: in the middle of the capital, inside the city of Chang'an. It does not mean China here.

glosses.zh: 箜篌：一种古代弹拨乐器，有点像竖琴。
glosses.en: kōng hóu: an ancient plucked instrument, a bit like a harp.

glosses.zh: 昆山玉碎：昆山就是昆仑山，出产美玉。这里形容乐声清脆，像美玉碎裂的声音。
glosses.en: kūn shān yù suì: Kunshan is the Kunlun Mountains, famous for jade. The music is crisp and clear, like jade breaking.

glosses.zh: 凤凰叫：像凤凰鸣叫，形容乐声和美悠扬。
glosses.en: fèng huáng jiào: like the call of the phoenix, sweet and soaring.

glosses.zh: 芙蓉泣露：荷花上挂着露水，好像在哭泣，形容乐声低沉悲伤。
glosses.en: fú róng qì lù: dew on the lotus flowers looks like tears, so the music sounds low and sad.

glosses.zh: 香兰笑：兰花开放，好像在笑，形容乐声轻快欢乐。
glosses.en: xiāng lán xiào: the orchids open as if smiling, so the music sounds light and happy.

glosses.zh: 十二门：长安城四面各有三个城门，共十二个，代指整个长安城。
glosses.en: shí èr mén: the twelve gates. Chang'an had three gates on each side, twelve in all, standing for the whole city.

glosses.zh: 融冷光：深秋清冷的光好像都被音乐融化了，变得温暖。
glosses.en: róng lěng guāng: the cold light of late autumn seems to melt and turn warm in the music.

glosses.zh: 二十三丝：竖箜篌有二十三根弦。
glosses.en: èr shí sān sī: twenty-three strings; the upright harp had twenty-three.

glosses.zh: 紫皇：道教传说中天上最高的神，也暗指人间的皇帝。
glosses.en: zǐ huáng: the highest god in heaven in Daoist legend; it may also hint at the emperor.

glosses.zh: 女娲炼石补天：传说天塌了一块，女神女娲炼出五色石把天补好。
glosses.en: nǚ wā liàn shí bǔ tiān: legend says part of the sky fell in, and the goddess Nüwa melted five-colored stones to mend it.

glosses.zh: 石破天惊：补天的石头被乐声震破了，天也被惊动了。现在用来形容事情让人非常震惊。
glosses.en: shí pò tiān jīng: the mending stones crack and the sky is shaken by the music. Today the phrase means something truly astonishing.

glosses.zh: 逗：引出来。
glosses.en: dòu: to draw out, to bring on.

glosses.zh: 神山：神仙住的山。
glosses.en: shén shān: a mountain where gods and immortals live.

glosses.zh: 神妪：传说中善于弹箜篌的神仙老妇人。
glosses.en: shén yù: an old goddess in legend who played the konghou very well.

glosses.zh: 老鱼跳波瘦蛟舞：老鱼在水波中跳跃，瘦蛟龙也跳起舞来。古书里说，琴弹得好，鱼都会跳出水面来听。
glosses.en: lǎo yú tiào bō shòu jiāo wǔ: old fish leap from the waves and thin dragons dance. An old book says that when music is good enough, fish jump out of the water to listen.

glosses.zh: 吴质：就是吴刚，传说他在月亮上不停地砍桂树。
glosses.en: wú zhì: another name for Wu Gang, who in legend keeps chopping the cassia tree on the moon.

glosses.zh: 露脚：露水下落的样子，像露珠长了脚。
glosses.en: lù jiǎo: dew feet, the way dewdrops fall, as if they had feet.

glosses.zh: 寒兔：月亮里的玉兔，也代指月亮。
glosses.en: hán tù: the cold rabbit, the jade rabbit on the moon; it also stands for the moon.

translation.zh: 深秋时节，李凭弹起用吴丝蜀桐做成的箜篌，
translation.en: In deep autumn, Li Ping plays a harp of Wu silk and Shu tung wood.

translation.zh: 空旷的山中，云听到乐声凝住不动，垂着不再飘。
translation.en: Over the empty hills, the clouds hear it and stop, hanging still.

translation.zh: 江边的娥皇女英在斑竹上哭泣，素女也满面忧愁，
translation.en: The river goddesses weep on the bamboo, and the zither goddess grows sad,

translation.zh: 这是因为李凭在京城里弹奏箜篌。
translation.en: because Li Ping is playing his harp in the capital.

translation.zh: 乐声清脆，像昆仑山的美玉碎裂，又像凤凰在鸣叫；
translation.en: The music is like Kunlun jade shattering, like a phoenix calling;

translation.zh: 时而像荷花含露哭泣，时而像兰花开放欢笑。
translation.en: now like lotus flowers weeping dew, now like orchids smiling.

translation.zh: 长安城十二道城门前的清冷寒光，好像都被乐声融化了；
translation.en: Before Chang'an's twelve gates, the cold light melts away;

translation.zh: 二十三根弦的乐声，打动了天上的紫皇。
translation.en: the twenty-three strings move the Purple Emperor in heaven.

translation.zh: 乐声直冲到女娲炼石补天的地方，
translation.en: The sound flies up to where Nüwa mended the sky with stones.

translation.zh: 补天的石头被震破，天被惊动，引出了一场秋雨。
translation.en: The stones crack, the sky is startled, and autumn rain pours down.

translation.zh: 恍惚中，李凭好像梦见自己进了神山，把技艺教给神妪；
translation.en: It is as if Li Ping dreams he enters the gods' mountain and teaches the old goddess to play.

translation.zh: 老鱼在波浪中跳跃，瘦蛟龙也跟着起舞。
translation.en: Old fish leap in the waves, and thin dragons dance.

translation.zh: 月宫里的吴刚听得入迷，彻夜不睡，靠着桂树；
translation.en: On the moon, Wu Gang cannot sleep; he leans on the cassia tree, listening.

translation.zh: 露珠斜斜地飞落，打湿了寒冷的玉兔。
translation.en: Dewdrops fly slanting down and wet the cold moon rabbit.

background.zh: 李凭是唐宪宗时宫廷里有名的乐师，最擅长弹箜篌，当时很受人喜爱，不少诗人都写诗称赞过他的演奏。一般认为，这首诗是李贺在长安做奉礼郎（管祭祀礼仪的小官）时写的，大约在811到813年之间。他听了李凭的演奏，用一连串神奇的想象把听到的音乐“画”了出来。
background.en: Li Ping was a famous court musician in the time of Emperor Xianzong of Tang. He was best at the konghou harp and much loved in his day. Several poets wrote poems praising his playing. This poem is usually thought to have been written while Li He held a small post in Chang'an looking after ceremonies, around 811 to 813. After hearing Li Ping play, he used a string of magical images to paint the music in words.

author_note.zh: 李贺（790—816），字长吉，福昌（今河南宜阳）人，是唐朝皇族的远房后代。因为父亲名叫“晋肃”，“晋”和“进士”的“进”同音，有人说他应该避讳，他就没能参加进士考试。他一生不得志，只活了二十七岁（按古人算年龄的方法）。他的诗想象奇特，常写鬼神仙怪，被人称为“诗鬼”。
author_note.en: Li He (790–816), also called Changji, came from Fuchang, today's Yiyang in Henan. He was a distant relative of the Tang royal family. His father's name sounded like the word for the top civil exam, and people said he should avoid it out of respect, so he never took that exam. He never got ahead in life and died young, at twenty-seven by the old Chinese way of counting age. His poems are full of strange imagination, often about ghosts, gods and spirits, so he is called the Ghost of Poetry.

appreciation.zh: 音乐看不见、摸不着，怎么写？李贺的办法是：不直接写声音，而是写听到音乐的天地万物有什么反应。云停了，神女哭了，城门前的冷光化了，天上的神被打动了，连补天的石头都被震破，下起了秋雨。鱼跳起来，蛟龙跳起舞，月亮上的吴刚整夜不睡。“昆山玉碎凤凰叫，芙蓉泣露香兰笑”两句，一句写声音的清脆和高亢，一句写曲调的悲伤和欢快，有声音、有画面、有表情。整首诗像一场从人间飞到天上、又飞进月宫的旅行。读完你会觉得：这音乐真是好听极了。
appreciation.en: Music cannot be seen or touched, so how do you write about it? Li He's trick is not to describe the sound directly. Instead he shows how all of heaven and earth react to it. The clouds stop. The goddesses cry. The cold light at the city gates melts. The god in heaven is moved. Even the stones that mend the sky crack, and autumn rain falls. Fish leap, dragons dance, and Wu Gang on the moon stays awake all night. The two lines about jade shattering and lotus weeping work as a pair. One gives the music's crisp, high notes; the other gives its sad and happy moods. They have sound, pictures and feelings all at once. The whole poem is like a journey from earth up to the sky and into the moon palace. By the end, you feel this music must have been wonderful.
